final_message:
Both files now have the same correct implementation. The fix was to change `r"[^a-z0-9]"` to `r"[^a-z0-9]+"` in the regex pattern, which correctly matches sequences of non-alphanumeric characters (instead of individual ones).

The original bug was that the regex `[^a-z0-9]` (without the `+`) only matched single non-alphanumeric characters, resulting in multiple hyphens being inserted. The fix adds the `+` quantifier to match one or more consecutive non-alphanumeric characters as a single replacement.
